title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
authors: Carlos E. Jimenez; John Yang; Alexander Wettig; Shunyu Yao; Kexin Pei; Ofir Press; Karthik Narasimhan
central_claim: 2,294 issue/PR task instances from 12 Python repos; a patch is judged by executing the PR's tests; best model at the time (Claude 2) resolved 1.96%.
cite_claim: Origin of the execution-based fail-to-pass evaluation used by every issue-reproduction benchmark below.
quote: 2,294 software engineering problems drawn from real GitHub issues and corresponding pull requests across 12 popular Python repositories [verify exact wording]
relevance: Foundational definition of the F->P / P->P protocol that fiks's F and P gates mirror (fiks adds a stated-reason check SWE-bench lacks).

title: princeton-nlp/SWE-bench dataset card (FAIL_TO_PASS, PASS_TO_PASS fields)
authors: Princeton NLP (SWE-bench maintainers)
central_claim: FAIL_TO_PASS lists tests resolved by the PR and tied to the issue; PASS_TO_PASS lists tests that must pass before and after.
cite_claim: Operational definition of fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests in SWE-bench.
quote: A json list of strings that represent the set of tests resolved by the PR and tied to the issue resolution.
relevance: Exact wording for our F->P definition; fiks's P gate = FAIL_TO_PASS plus PASS_TO_PASS (full contract suite + stored traces).

title: princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified dataset card
authors: Princeton NLP; OpenAI (human validation)
central_claim: 500-instance human-validated subset of SWE-bench; evaluation by unit tests using post-PR behavior as reference.
cite_claim: SWE-bench needed human validation of its own F->P tests; even curated benchmark tests are not automatically valid oracles.
quote: SWE-bench Verified is a subset of 500 samples from the SWE-bench test set, which have been human-validated for quality.
relevance: Shows test validity is a known problem even for human-written F->P tests. OpenAI's announcement page (filter reasons) returned 403 and is NOT cited.

title: Large Language Models are Few-shot Testers: Exploring LLM-based General Bug Reproduction
authors: Sungmin Kang; Juyeon Yoon; Shin Yoo
central_claim: First LLM issue-to-test approach: 33% (251/750) of Defects4J reports reproduced; 32% on 31 post-cutoff reports; stack traces help crash bugs (84 vs 69 reproduced).
cite_claim: Foundational LLM bug-report-to-test result; adding stack traces to the report increased reproduced crash bugs from 69 to 84.
location: Abstract; Sec. VI-A1 and Table III (stack traces); Sec. I (96% statistic citing Koyuncu et al.)
quote: LIBRO can generate failure reproducing test cases for 33% of all studied cases (251 out of 750)
relevance: Baseline lineage; the stack-trace ablation is the closest published evidence that runtime artifacts make LLM reproduction easier (supports C19 partially).

title: SWT-Bench: Testing and Validating Real-World Bug-Fixes with Code Agents
authors: Niels Mündler; Mark Niklas Müller; Jingxuan He; Martin Vechev
central_claim: 1,983-instance benchmark for issue-to-test; success = at least one F->P test and no x->F test; best method SWE-Agent+ 18.5% on Lite; generated tests double SWE-Agent patch precision to 47.8% at 20% recall.
cite_claim: Standard reproduction-test metric and the finding that code agents write F->P tests for under one fifth of Lite issues; F->P counts any thrown error (including syntax errors) as a failure.
location: Sec. 3.1 (definition); Table 2 (S rates); Sec. 5.3 (filtering); Table 3 (change coverage)
quote: contains at least one F→P test and no ×→F test
relevance: Primary benchmark and metric; its failure definition does not check failure cause, which is exactly the gap fiks's stated-reason F gate addresses.

title: logic-star-ai/swt-bench (evaluation harness)
authors: LogicStar AI / ETH SRI Lab
central_claim: MIT-licensed Docker harness for SWT-Bench (Lite/Verified); supports unit-test and reproduction-script modes; needs ~120GB disk.
cite_claim: Runnable baseline harness to calibrate our LLM test generator against published F->P numbers.
quote: Evaluation harness for SWT-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM repository-level test-generation
relevance: Candidate external benchmark/baseline; license MIT.

title: TDD-Bench Verified: Can LLMs Generate Tests for Issues Before They Get Resolved?
authors: Toufique Ahmed; Martin Hirzel; Rangeet Pan; Avraham Shinnar; Saurabh Sinha
central_claim: 449-issue benchmark filtered from SWE-bench Verified by human judges and execution; tests should be fail-to-pass and cover the changed code.
cite_claim: Second standard F->P benchmark; adds coverage adequacy of the golden change to the F->P criterion.
quote: a high-quality benchmark suite of 449 issues mined from real-world GitHub code repositories
relevance: Benchmark; its harness (Apache-2.0) is runnable.

title: IBM/TDD-Bench-Verified (evaluation harness)
authors: IBM Research
central_claim: Apache-2.0 Docker harness reporting TDD_Score and fail-to-pass count for 449 instances.
cite_claim: Runnable F->P harness for external calibration.
quote: TDD-Bench-Verified is a new benchmark for generating test cases for test-driven development (TDD)
relevance: Candidate baseline harness.

title: Otter: Generating Tests from Issues to Validate SWE Patches
authors: Toufique Ahmed; Jatin Ganhotra; Rangeet Pan; Avraham Shinnar; Saurabh Sinha; Martin Hirzel
central_claim: LLM + rule-based checking/repair + planner: 31.4% (Otter) and 37.0% (Otter++) F->P on TDD-Bench-Verified with GPT-4o; tests with Error failures are F->P only 3.7% of the time vs 57.1% for assertion failures; filtering raises a leaderboard system's precision 60.8%->91.9% at 33% recall.
cite_claim: Failure type predicts validity: assertion-failing tests are far more often true F->P than error-failing tests; generated tests are high-precision, low-recall patch filters.
location: Table 1; Table 3; Table 6 and Sec. 4.2; Sec. 6.7
quote: maximize the chance that it failed for the right reason
relevance: Empirical basis for fiks requiring an AssertionError naming the violated property (not any error) in the F gate.

title: Heterogeneous Prompting and Execution Feedback for SWE Issue Test Generation and Selection
authors: Toufique Ahmed; Jatin Ganhotra; Avraham Shinnar; Martin Hirzel
central_claim: Execution feedback from running candidate tests on old code, plus an LLM critic judging whether a test fails for the right reason, reaches 63.0% F->P on TDD-Bench-Verified (Claude 3.7 Sonnet); removing the critic drops 37.2%->29.4% (GPT-4o); critic F-score 0.78-0.83.
cite_claim: Runtime execution information about the old code measurably improves LLM reproduction-test generation; wrong-reason failure is judged by an LLM critic with F-score ~0.8.
quote: a test may not fail for the reason mentioned in the issue description
relevance: Strongest current issue-to-test system; its LLM critic is the probabilistic counterpart of fiks's deterministic stated-reason check; supports C19 direction (execution info helps).

title: Reproduction Test Generation for Java SWE Issues
authors: Toufique Ahmed; Jatin Ganhotra; Avraham Shinnar; Martin Hirzel
central_claim: TDD-Bench-Java (250 instances); e-Otter++ 43.6% (Claude Sonnet 4.5) / 46.4% (GPT-5.2) F->P; on 150 proprietary issues F->P was 4% from default descriptions and 20% with identifier hints.
cite_claim: On industrial issues with prose-only reports, LLM reproduction yield collapsed to 4% and rose to 20% when precise code identifiers were added.
location: Sec. 3.1-3.2; Sec. 4.1 (critic); Sec. 5.2 Finding 1; Sec. 6.2 Finding 5; Table 5
quote: whether the test is failing for the right reason: the problem described in the issue description
relevance: Best evidence that report precision drives reproduction yield (supports C19's premise that a captured call is better input than prose); also shows benchmark-to-industry drop.

title: Issue2Test: Generating Reproducing Test Cases from Issue Reports
authors: Noor Nashid; Islem Bouzenia; Michael Pradel; Ali Mesbah
central_claim: Iteratively refines tests with compilation/runtime feedback until they fail for the issue's reason; 32.9% of SWT-bench-lite reproduced (Claude 3.5 Sonnet); failure-reason check is LLM-based.
cite_claim: Explicitly targets tests that fail for the reason described in the issue, checked by an LLM categorization prompt; no systematic count of wrong-reason failures is reported.
location: Abstract; Sec. 2.5 Alg. 1; Fig. 9; Table 2; Sec. 3.2.4
quote: a test that fails, and that fails specifically for the reason described in the issue
relevance: Closest definitional match to fiks's F gate; numbers differ across arXiv versions (cite v4).

title: AEGIS: An Agent-based Framework for General Bug Reproduction from Issue Descriptions
authors: Xinchen Wang; Pengfei Gao; Xiangxin Meng; Chao Peng; Ruida Hu; Yun Lin; Cuiyun Gao
central_claim: Context construction + FSM-guided script generation for general bug reproduction scripts; beats the best baseline by 23.0% on F->P and raises Agentless relative resolved rate by 12.5%.
cite_claim: Agentic reproduction-script generation with constrained (FSM) actions improves F->P and downstream resolution.
quote: outperforms the state-of-the-art baseline by 23.0% in F->P metric [verify; an FSE listing summary reported 19.0%]
relevance: Reproduction scripts (not unit tests) as repair input; number discrepancy between versions flagged.

title: Agentic Bug Reproduction for Effective Automated Program Repair at Google
authors: Runxiang Cheng; Michele Tufano; Jürgen Cito; José Cambronero; Pat Rondon; Renyao Wei; Aaron Sun; Satish Chandra
central_claim: On 80 Google bugs, BRT Agent: 85% candidate (fails on buggy) vs 28% plausible (F->P) BRTs; LIBRO 41%/10%; giving BRTs to APR gave 17/23 vs 13/23 bugs with plausible fixes (+30% relative).
cite_claim: In industry, failing-on-buggy is necessary but not sufficient: only about a third of candidate reproduction tests are F->P; BRTs raise APR plausible-fix rate.
quote: necessary, but not sufficient
relevance: Industrial evidence for C17-type bottleneck and for repro-before-repair; inputs were issue text only, so it does not test traces.

title: Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair
authors: Runxiang Cheng; Michele Tufano; José Cambronero; Renyao Wei; Sherry Shi; Grant Uy; Pat Rondon; Franjo Ivančić
central_claim: Co-generating fix and BRT in one agent (120 Google bugs, 6 languages) matches separate generation on each and beats both on fix-and-BRT; agents bias fixes toward their own BRTs and sometimes delete BRTs.
cite_claim: When the same agent writes test and fix, fixes can be biased toward the agent's own test, and BRT plausibility is unknown at deployment without an oracle fix.
location: Sec. 1; Sec. 4.2.1; Sec. 5.1; Sec. 5.3.1; Sec. 6; Table 6
quote: The agent sometimes implements a fix biased towards its own BRT, or vice versa.
relevance: Motivates fiks's separation: repro generated before repair, frozen, and the repair agent cannot edit it.

title: ReProAgent: Tool-Augmented Multi-Stage Agentic Generation of Bug Reproduction Tests from Issue Reports
authors: Quanjun Zhang; Yi Zheng; Ye Shang; Weifeng Sun; Haichuan Hu; Chunrong Fang; Zhenyu Chen; Liang Xiao
central_claim: Four-stage agent (localize, root-cause, assertion-aware plan, test + triadic review) with GPT-5-mini: 58.43% FP on SWT-bench-lite, 70.30% on SWT-bench-verified; removing execution-feedback review drops lite 56.88%->18.84%; correct localization 50.7%->67.8%.
cite_claim: Latest SOTA issue-to-test agent; execution feedback and correct localization are the largest contributors to F->P rate.
quote: A failing test, however, is not immediately accepted as a valid reproduction.
relevance: Upper bound of prose-to-test today (~58-70% on curated Python benchmarks); text/table disagreement on best baseline (38.0 vs 40.2) flagged.

title: Multi-SWT-Bench: A Multilingual Benchmark for Reproduction Test Generation
authors: Kazuki Kusama; Sota Nakashima; Haruka Tokumasu; Masanari Kondo; Lingming Zhang; Yasutaka Kamei
central_claim: 1,963 instances in 8 languages (incl. TypeScript, JavaScript); all LLMs trigger a failure in >80% of instances but F->P is 9.7-28.5 pp lower than F->x; best F->P 79.41% (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5); later agent revisions can invalidate working reproduction tests.
cite_claim: Fail-on-buggy rates overstate reproduction: many generated failures are not resolved by the golden patch; agent edits can silently break a previously valid reproduction.
location: Table 1; Sec. 2.1; Sec. 4.1.2; Sec. 4.2.1-4.2.2; Table 4; Appendix C
quote: subsequent revisions can invalidate a previously working reproduction test
relevance: Most recent and TypeScript-inclusive benchmark; documents wrong-reason failure cases; strongest current numbers for agent repro (a reviewer will cite it).

title: TDFlow: Agentic Workflows for Test Driven Software Engineering
authors: Kevin Han et al. (CMU, UCSD, JHU)
central_claim: Given human-written tests, 88.8% (Lite) and 94.3% (Verified) resolution; with LLM-generated tests 68.0% on Verified (Table 2; Sec. 1 says 69.8%); 7 test-hacking cases in 800 manually reviewed runs.
cite_claim: Existing claim C17: the bottleneck is writing valid reproduction tests, not solving them.
location: Abstract; Tables 1-2; Sec. 1; Sec. 4.2; Sec. 4.4; Sec. 5; Appendix C
quote: the primary bottleneck to human-level software engineering performance lies within writing tests rather than solving them
relevance: C17. NOTE: internal inconsistency 68.0% (Table 2) vs 69.8% (Sec. 1); README/RESEARCH should cite Table 2 and say so.

title: SWE-Doctor: Guiding Software Engineering Agents with Runtime Diagnosis from Multi-Faceted Bug Reproduction Tests
authors: Yaoqi Guo; Yang Liu; Jie M. Zhang; Yun Ma; Yiling Lou; Zhenpeng Chen
central_claim: Guiding agents with SOTA BRTs does not reliably help: fail-to-fail BRTs mislead, F->P BRTs give limited or negative gains; multi-faceted BRTs turned into runtime diagnoses reach 75.7% (Verified) and 59.4% (Pro).
cite_claim: Existing claim C20: a single F->P test may cover one manifestation and lead to partial patches.
quote: fail-to-pass BRTs may cover only one manifestation of the reported issue, leading to partial patches
relevance: C20; strongest counter-evidence that a repro test alone improves repair; also shows runtime diagnosis helps.

title: Investigating Test Overfitting on SWE-bench
authors: Toufique Ahmed; Jatin Ganhotra; Avraham Shinnar; Martin Hirzel
central_claim: 21.8% (Claude 3.7) and 33.0% (GPT-4o) of patches passing generated tests fail hidden golden tests; refinement against the tests raises overfitting to 25.5%/35.9%; revealing golden tests drops it to 5.8%/11.3%.
cite_claim: Passing a generated reproduction test is a weak correctness signal; iterating against it increases overfitting.
location: Sec. 2; Table 1; Sec. 4.2; Table 3; Sec. 5; Sec. 7
quote: Test overfitting happens when an system generates code that passes observed tests but fails held-out hidden tests.
relevance: Defines the overfitting risk fiks's held-out checks (full contract suite, all stored traces, withheld repro variants) must measure.

title: Failure Reproducing Test Case Generation Method Based on Large Language Model
authors: Ying Wang; Qian Cheng Zi; Xin Peng; Yi Ling Lou
venue_or_publisher: Ruan Jian Xue Bao / Journal of Software 37(4):1690-1714
central_claim: Nearly 90% of SWE-bench Lite issues lack failure-reproducing tests; issues lack the stack traces crash-reproduction methods depend on, so the method gathers code context instead.
cite_claim: Existing claim C18: ~90% of SWE-bench Lite issues are submitted without a failure-reproducing test.
quote: nearly 90% of issues are submitted without failure reproducing test cases
relevance: C18; also states the stack-trace dependency of prior methods (silent failures have no stack trace either).

title: Search-Based Crash Reproduction and Its Impact on Debugging
authors: Mozhan Soltani; Annibale Panichella; Arie van Deursen
central_claim: Guided genetic algorithm seeded by the stack trace reproduces crashes (54 real-world crashes studied); developers with EvoCrash tests fixed more often and faster.
cite_claim: Classical crash reproduction uses the runtime stack trace as both search guide and oracle; reproduced tests measurably help human debugging.
quote: EvoCrash outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in crash reproduction
relevance: Prior art for 'runtime artifact -> reproduction'; requires a crash, which silent tool failures do not produce. JCrashPack 43% figure seen only in search snippets [verify].

title: Botsing, a Search-based Crash Reproduction Framework for Java
authors: Pouria Derakhshanfar; Xavier Devroey; Annibale Panichella; Andy Zaidman; Arie van Deursen
central_claim: Open-source, extensible EvoSuite-based framework that generates crash-reproducing tests from stack traces; evaluated on open-source and industrial crashes.
cite_claim: Open-source stack-trace-to-test tooling exists for crashes (Java).
quote: easy-to-extend framework [verify exact phrase]
relevance: Crash-reproduction tool lineage; not applicable as a baseline (Java, crash oracle).

title: BugRedux: Reproducing Field Failures for In-house Debugging
authors: Wei Jin; Alessandro Orso
central_claim: Symbolic execution guided by field execution data synthesizes in-house runs that mimic field failures; recreated 17 failures in 15 real programs with a limited set of execution data.
cite_claim: Field-collected execution data makes failure reproduction feasible; the question is how little data suffices.
quote: suitable yet limited set of execution data
relevance: Closest classical analogue of C19 (field trace -> reproduction); fiks records the full upstream exchange, so it sits at the 'collect more, replay exactly' end of BugRedux's trade-off.

title: ReCDroid: Automatically Reproducing Android Application Crashes from Bug Reports
authors: Yu Zhao; Tingting Yu; Ting Su; Yang Liu; Wei Zheng; Jingzhi Zhang; William G.J. Halfond
central_claim: NLP + guided GUI exploration reproduced 33 of 51 Android crash reports (63.5%) from text alone.
cite_claim: Pre-LLM report-to-reproduction for mobile crashes reached ~64% on its benchmark.
quote: ReCDroid successfully reproduced 33 crashes (63.5% success rate) directly from the textual description of bug reports
relevance: Crash-reproduction lineage (named in task).

title: Prompting Is All You Need: Automated Android Bug Replay with Large Language Models
authors: Sidong Feng; Chunyang Chen
central_claim: LLM prompting replays 81.3% of Android bug reports in about 254 s on average.
cite_claim: LLMs substantially improved report-to-replay for Android over ReCDroid-era tools.
quote: reproduce 81.3% of bug reports in 253.6 seconds
relevance: Shows reproduction yield depends strongly on domain; mobile replay with an observable crash is easier than general logic bugs.

title: CrashJS: A NodeJS Benchmark for Automated Crash Reproduction
authors: Philip Oliver; Jens Dietrich; Craig Anslow; Michael Homer
central_claim: 453 Node.js crashes collected as a crash-reproduction benchmark.
cite_claim: A JavaScript/Node crash-reproduction benchmark exists; it targets crashes, not silent wrong results.
quote: benchmark dataset of 453 Node.js crashes [verify exact wording]
relevance: Same runtime as MCP TypeScript servers; possible source of comparison cases, but crash-only.

title: Engineering Record And Replay For Deployability: Extended Technical Report
authors: Robert O'Callahan; Chris Jones; Nathan Froyd; Kyle Huey; Albert Noll; Nimrod Partush
central_claim: Practical user-space record/replay (rr) with low overhead supports reverse debugging and reproducing hard-to-find test failures.
cite_claim: Recording nondeterministic inputs at a boundary and replaying them is an established route to deterministic failure reproduction.
quote: record and replay program executions with low overhead enables many applications
relevance: Process-level record/replay ancestor of fiks's HTTP-boundary record/replay; rr records everything, fiks records only the upstream HTTP boundary.

title: VCR (Ruby): record and replay HTTP interactions
authors: VCR maintainers
central_claim: Records a test suite's HTTP interactions to cassettes and replays them for fast, deterministic tests; cassettes can be re-recorded on an interval.
cite_claim: HTTP cassette record/replay is the standard engineering practice fiks's fixtures follow.
quote: Record your test suite's HTTP interactions and replay them during future test runs for fast, deterministic, accurate tests.
relevance: Engineering precedent; fiks's novelty is not record/replay but recording at violation time and pairing the cassette with a contract oracle.

title: Polly.JS
authors: Netflix
central_claim: Framework-agnostic JS library for recording, replaying and stubbing HTTP interactions in Node and browser; persists to disk or local storage.
cite_claim: Node/JS HTTP record/replay library (Apache-2.0).
quote: a standalone, framework-agnostic JavaScript library that enables recording, replaying, and stubbing of HTTP interactions
relevance: Possible drop-in for fiks's replay layer in TS MCP servers; candidate for the 'snapshot test from traffic' baseline.

title: nock: HTTP server mocking and expectations library for Node.js
authors: Pedro Teixeira and contributors
central_claim: Records live HTTP calls (recorder.rec, output_objects) and replays them; Nock Back fixtures with record / dryrun / lockdown modes.
cite_claim: Node HTTP recording with a lockdown mode that forbids unrecorded calls (analogous to fiks's UNMATCHED_REQUEST).
quote: use recorded nocks, disables all http calls even when not nocked, doesn't record
relevance: Precedent for strict replay; candidate library for the snapshot baseline.

title: Keploy: record API traffic as tests and dependency mocks
authors: Keploy Inc.
central_claim: Captures live API calls at the socket level (eBPF on Linux), generates tests and dependency mocks, replays them deterministically and compares responses to the captured ones.
cite_claim: Industry tool that turns real traffic into regression tests with recorded dependency mocks; its oracle is equality with the recorded response.
location: What is Keploy (docs); GitHub README ('convert real API calls into tests and mocks')
quote: Keploy will intercept and provide the previously recorded dependency response
relevance: Closest industrial analogue to fiks's capture->test step. Key difference: a recorded-response oracle encodes the buggy output, so it cannot yield an F->P repro for a silent fault; fiks's oracle is the contract.

title: An Empirical Analysis of Flaky Tests
authors: Qingzhou Luo; Farah Hariri; Lamyaa Eloussi; Darko Marinov
central_claim: 201 flaky-test-fixing commits in 51 projects; top root causes Async Wait (45% of 161 classified), Concurrency (20%), Test Order Dependency (12%); network and time are listed causes.
cite_claim: Nondeterminism from async waits, network and time is the main source of flaky tests, motivating replay of recorded upstream responses and multi-run determinism checks.
quote: The top three categories of flaky tests are Async Wait, Concurrency, and Test Order Dependency.
relevance: Justifies fiks's F gate requiring identical failures on 3/3 runs over recorded fixtures.
